assessment.headline: DAY 34. Trump's address was NOT peace — it was 'stone ages for 2-3 more weeks.' And he won't secure Hormuz. India is on its own.
assessment.body:
Trump's prime-time address was the most consequential moment of the war for India — and the news is bad. He said objectives are 'nearing completion' but will hit Iran 'EXTREMELY HARD for 2-3 more weeks.' Oil jumped 4% immediately after. Asian markets fell. The relief rally evaporated.

The worst part for India: Trump explicitly said the US will NOT secure the Strait of Hormuz. 'Countries must take care of that passage.' 'The strait will open up naturally.' This means India, Japan, and South Korea are on their own. The UK is hosting a 35-nation conference on Hormuz, but Iran has already approved permanent tolls.

India's fuel position (verified from PIB, Apr 1):
• 60 days of stock cover (74-day total capacity)
• LPG: 30+ days. Production up 40% to 50,000 MT/day
• 800 TMT of LPG cargoes secured from US, Russia, Australia
• 41+ crude suppliers. Refineries at >100% utilization
• ZERO dry-outs reported at any pump or distributor
• But: Indian basket at $115.75/barrel. Excise cut absorbed by OMCs. Nayara hiked ₹5.30

Iran's death toll revised sharply: HRANA reports 3,519 killed — far higher than Red Crescent's 2,000+. Pentagon confirmed 348 US troops wounded. Hegseth says 'upcoming days will be decisive.'

The critical question: If Trump exits in 2-3 weeks without securing Hormuz, what happens? Iran keeps the toll. India pays permanently higher energy costs. The pre-war world of free Hormuz passage is over. India must now build a coalition — with Japan, South Korea, and possibly the UK — to secure its own energy supply lines. This is the new reality.
